messages:
Mara: noticing slow memory drift on a handful of >20k token sessions. GPU process RSS climbs ~30-50MB per 10k tokens for a subset of runs.
Sanjay: is this new? did we change compaction heuristics recently?
Mara: yes, saw the trend after the partial-compact change. I have a small repro harness `tests/long_context/slot_stress.py` that steadily shows allocation deltas.
bench-bot: profiler snapshot: kv_slot_alloc delta =~ +32MB/10k tokens; kv_fragment_count rises by ~1.2k per session. Attached flamegraphs in PR.
Jon: can we make this visible via metrics/dashboards, not just heap dumps? Ops needs a way to catch it early.
Mara: proposal: expose aggregated residency + eviction metrics by model/device/seq_bucket. Don't add session_id as a metric label (cardinality), but sample session traces.
Ellie: agree on cardinality. We should use fixed seq length buckets and device/model labels only. Emit occasional trace events that include session_id for deep dives.
Sanjay: metric set idea: `redwood_kv_residency_percent{model,device,seq_bucket}` gauge (sampled every 10s), `redwood_kv_evictions_total{model,device,age_bucket}` counter, `redwood_kv_fragment_reuse_ratio{model}` gauge (rolling 5m), `redwood_kv_compact_ops_total{model,device}` counter.
Mara: also want a histogram for resident slot counts: `redwood_kv_resident_slots_bucket` with buckets: 0-1k,1k-5k,5k-20k,20k+. That helps spot long-session cohorts.
Jon: add an alert: if model-level residency increases >10% over 1h while evictions_total remains below expected threshold => paging-leak alert. Another alert: sustained fragment_reuse_ratio < 0.6 for 30m.
Mara: sample log lines I captured:
```
[2026-03-17T14:21:02Z] session=abc123 tokens=12000 slots_alloc=34120 slots_resident=32890 fragments=4127 kv_slot_alloc_delta=+33MB
[2026-03-17T14:22:10Z] session=abc123 tokens=16000 slots_alloc=36300 slots_resident=35140 fragments=4253 kv_slot_alloc_delta=+31MB
```
bench-bot: kernel timings show compaction increases tail latency; p50 unchanged, p99 +~40ms during compaction.
Ellie: ops constraints: do not export session_id as a prometheus label. Use trace events: `kv_residency_snapshot` with session_id when sampled. Limit to 1 in N long sessions to keep traces sparse.
Sanjay: implementation plan (small PR):
- instrument runtime to emit `redwood_kv_residency_percent` gauge by model/device/seq_bucket every 10s
- increment `redwood_kv_evictions_total{age_bucket}` on eviction
- measure `redwood_kv_fragment_reuse_ratio` as reused_fragments / total_frag_ops over rolling window
- emit ephemeral trace events `kv_residency_sample` with session_id for sampled long sessions
Jon: +1. Also want a dashboard folder `Runtime / KV Observability` with panels: cluster residency heatmap, per-model eviction rate, fragment reuse over time, long-session cohort panel (heap delta vs tokens).
Mara: I'll open PR with the instrumentation + a draft Grafana dashboard JSON. Plan to run our long-context stress job in staging for 24h after rollout to validate no more steady growth.
deploy-bot: linked PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4891 passed CI and started staged rollout.
Ellie: devops reminder: keep seq_bucket fixed set to avoid explosion. Also record `compact_op_count` so we can correlate compaction runs with residency changes.
Mara: I'll add a small sampler (1%) that attaches session_id in traces for long sessions and include a debug endpoint to request a full residency snapshot for a given session (trace-driven).
Sanjay: after merge, run `tests/long_context/slot_stress.py --duration 24h --residency-logging` against staging fleet and collect metrics.
Jon: happy to help design the dashboard layout. Ping when dashboard draft is in the PR.
Mara: thanks, will send PR link in this thread once opened.
